A web application allows users to create and manage their own private forums. However, a developer accidentally added an "admin" parameter to the URL query string for one of the forum management pages, which is not validated or sanitized on the server-side. If a user were to append "?admin=true" to the URL, they would gain access to administrative functionality even if they don't have the necessary permissions.

Example code snippet:
```python
@app.route('/forums/<forum_id>/manage', methods=['GET'])
def manage_forum(forum_id):
    if request.args.get('admin') == 'true':
        # Admin-only functionality here
        pass
    # Rest of the logic...
```
In this scenario, a user could potentially browse to `http://example.com/forums/<forum_id>/manage?admin=true` and gain unauthorized access to administrative features.

Analyze this situation.

Fix: Deny by default; enforce authorization server-side on EVERY request; check record ownership; centralize access-control logic; never rely on client-side enforcement or hidden fields.
What to look for: Application-layer weakness in the class Broken Access Control.
